survivors.label: required_gap
survivors.reason: The package-level send_group_notification signature is explicitly required to default ttl to 0. The witness changes it to 1, serializes the payload and passes the resulting TTL positionally to the group utility, which forwards it to each matching subscription. A valid nonempty group called without ttl receives TTL 1. The recorded group success cases supply ttl=1000; a no-TTL missing-group call raises before dispatch and cannot establish the valid-group default.
evidence_refs: /Users/petermakhnatch/Developer/eval-lab/derived/qa/ref-subset/packages/mimo-v2.6-rl-code/format-code-task-002555/instruction.md:5: "The package-level API should include `send_user_notification(user, payload, ttl=0) -> None` and `send_group_notification(group_name, payload, ttl=0, exclude_user_id=None) -> None`. Both helpers should accept any JSON-serializable payload object, encode it with `json.dumps`, and forward that encoded payload with the given TTL to every matching subscription. For example, `send_user_notification(user, {\"head\": \"Welcome!\", \"body\": \"Hello World\"}, ttl=1000)` should send the JSON string for that payload to each subscription associated with `user`, and return `None` after dispatching. A payload such as `{\"head\": \"Welcome!\", \"body\": \"Hello World\", \"icon\": \"https://example.com/icon.png\", \"url\": \"https://example.com\"}` should preserve all keys and values in the JSON sent downstream."

only(x)

```

The extra information provided by the former is often enough to determine the fix for a bug simply by reading the exception message.

The downside of `get_only`'s approach is that it can produce large error messages for collections with large, complex objects with bulky `__repr__`s.
